title: Discovering and Mitigating Visual Biases through Keyword Explanation

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting common keywords from captions of misclassified images (e.g., CelebA) or generated images (e.g., Stable Diffusion) and measuring their similarity to the images using vision-language scoring models (like CLIP) to identify spurious correlations between gender and specific attributes or occupations.
Applying the Bias-to-Text (B2T) framework to the Dollar Street dataset to extract and analyze keywords associated with classifier mispredictions on objects originating from low-income countries.

Evaluating text-to-image generative models by extracting and scoring keywords from generated images to uncover racial stereotypes spuriously correlated with specific prompt conditions (e.g., occupations).

Using vision-language models to extract descriptive keywords that reveal spurious correlations between target classes and their backgrounds or surrounding contexts in datasets like Waterbirds and ImageNet.
